requirement: Serve POST /notes with aiohttp.web, validating the JSON body, title and tags and answering each problem with a 400 JSON error, and on success store the note and answer 201 with its id and Location.
skeleton: A typed AppKey for the note store, a 400 helper, create_note validating JSON, object shape, title and tags before storing and returning 201, and make_app wiring the route.
caption: A validated JSON create endpoint in aiohttp.web. NOTES_KEY is a typed web.AppKey holding the note list, and make_app registers POST /notes with an empty store. create_note(request) awaits request.json and answers every bad input with a 400 JSON error body instead of raising: invalid JSON, including an empty body, says body must be valid JSON, and anything but an object says body must be a JSON object. title must be a non-blank string, else title is required, and at most MAX_TITLE_CHARS, 100, characters. tags defaults to an empty list and must be a list of strings. A valid note gets id len(notes) + 1, the stripped title and the tags, is appended to the store, and returns status 201 with a Location header /notes/<id>. The fixture asserts, over an aiohttp TestServer, that two notes get ids 1 and 2 with stripped titles, default tags and Location headers, that 100 characters pass and 101 fail with the length message, that broken JSON, an array and an empty body are 400, that missing, blank or numeric titles are 400, and that a string or mixed tags list is 400 with nothing stored.

plan.intent: Accept user-submitted notes without crashing on bad input
constraints: Invalid or empty JSON and non-object bodies answer 400 with an error message
title is a non-blank string of at most 100 characters and is stored stripped
tags defaults to an empty list and must contain only strings
Success answers 201 with the note and a Location header

rationale.teaches: Validate request.json output explicitly, return structured 400 responses, and signal creation with 201 and Location.
rationale.why: Unchecked payload shapes turn client mistakes into 500 errors, loose element checks store bad data, and 200 without Location hides where the resource lives.

ops.docstring: A JSON create endpoint for aiohttp.web with explicit validation.

ops.source:
def _bad_request(message: str) -> web.Response:
    return web.json_response({"error": message}, status=400)

def make_app() -> web.Application:
    """Build the application with an empty note store."""
    app = web.Application()
    app[NOTES_KEY] = []
    app.router.add_post("/notes", create_note)
    return app

candidates.why_wrong: A title of exactly 100 characters is rejected.
A JSON array reaches payload.get and the handler crashes with a 500.
Tag lists containing numbers are stored instead of rejected.
The title is stored with its surrounding whitespace.
